answers.q1: Bundler with Rake. The root Gemfile and Rakefile drive the main project. Install with: bundle install. sinatra-contrib and rack-protection have their own Gemfiles, so also run: (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle install) and (cd rack-protection && bundle install)
answers.q2: bundle exec rake && (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rake) && (cd rack-protection && bundle exec rake). The root default task runs the Minitest suite in test/. CI runs these same three suites in test.yml.
answers.q4: CI runs no lint or formatting step (.github/workflows/test.yml only runs the rake test suites). The closest match is the RuboCop configured in .rubocop.yml, run from the root with: bundle exec rubocop
answers.q5: sinatra-contrib/sinatra-contrib.gemspec is generated: the 'sinatra-contrib.gemspec' rake task rewrites its authors, email and files lists from git. Regenerate it with: (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rake sinatra-contrib.gemspec). Per the root Rakefile, the VERSION constants in lib/sinatra/version.rb, sinatra-contrib/lib/sinatra/contrib/version.rb and rack-protection/lib/rack/protection/version.rb are rewritten by rake release:commit_version from the VERSION file, so change the VERSION file rather than those constants. doc/ and pkg/ are rake build outputs. No vendored directories were found.

q1.reason: Gives `bundle install` and correctly notes the subprojects have their own Gemfiles.

q2.reason: `bundle exec rake` matches, and the extra sub-suite commands match what CI runs.

q3.reason: `(cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rspec spec/capture_spec.rb)` is equivalent to the accepted command.

q4.reason: States CI runs no lint and gives `bundle exec rubocop` as the local check.

q5.reason: Mentions doc/ and pkg/ build outputs and says no vendored dirs, but claims sinatra-contrib.gemspec and version constants are generated, which the truth does not support and doesn't name coverage/.
